## Introduction

Lab 6 uses an STM32L432KC to read a DS1722 temperature sensor over SPI and communicate with an ESP8266 over UART. The webpage displays temperature and LED status, lets the user toggle the LED, and provides 8–12-bit temperature resolution settings.

The source code is available in the [Lab 6 GitHub repository](https://github.com/thivenanderson/E155-Lab6). The design follows the [Lab 6 specifications](https://hmc-e155.github.io/lab/lab6/specs.html).

## Hardware

The DS1722 uses SPI1 with PA5 (SCK), PA6 (MISO), PA7 (MOSI), and PA4 (CE). The ESP8266 communicates over USART1 at 125000 baud using PA9 (TX) and PA10 (RX), with TX and RX crossed between devices. The ESP8266 requires 3.3 V power. PB3 controls the on-board LED.

## Software and Microcontroller Design

The SPI driver uses the STM32 CMSIS register definitions to configure SPI1 as a master with 8-bit transfers, CPOL = 0, and CPHA = 1. It polls the transmit and receive flags to exchange one byte at a time.

The DS1722 driver controls CE, configures continuous conversion, and reads the temperature's two bytes. They are combined into a signed 16-bit value and divided by 256 to obtain degrees Celsius, including negative temperatures.

The STM32 receives webpage requests from the ESP8266 over UART and returns HTML containing the latest temperature and LED state. Resolution buttons send requests that update the DS1722 configuration register.

<details>
<summary>SPI transfer function</summary>

```c
char spiSendReceive(char send) {
    while (!(SPI1->SR & SPI_SR_TXE));
    *(__IO uint8_t *)&SPI1->DR = (uint8_t)send;

    while (!(SPI1->SR & SPI_SR_RXNE));
    return *(__IO uint8_t *)&SPI1->DR;
}
```

</details>

## Requirements Verification

The firmware builds in SEGGER and includes the CMSIS SPI driver, signed temperature conversion, webpage LED controls, and 8–12-bit resolution selection. The signed reading format supports temperatures below zero, including the required −10°C to 30°C range.
